counterfactual_classification.method: A repeat is retaliatory when the same rival selected a hostile action against odin free after the preceding mark and before the repeat.

official_rule_evidence.target_mark_semantics: The OpenFront English game text says a target mark is visible to all allies and coordinates attacks.
official_rule_evidence.execution_effect: TargetPlayerExecution decreases the target player's relation toward the requestor by 40.
official_rule_evidence.relation_bounds: Relations clamp to [-100, 100], so three unopposed marks can reach maximum hostility from neutral.
official_rule_evidence.cooldown_and_duration: A mark lasts 100 ticks and the action cools down for 150 ticks; repeated legal marks are new escalation pulses, not simultaneous duplicates.

rci.problem: When no tactical or stable alliance action remained, qd1n repeatedly marked the largest rival even without new hostility, creating an avoidable relation penalty in recurring losing profiles.
rci.smallest_fix: Keep one live campaign target. Permit a new target after the old target is eliminated or allied, and permit a repeat only after that rival attacks qd1n again.
preserved_boundaries: All tactical actions and stable survival alliances keep their existing priority.
Allies, reciprocal partners, and fresh alliance-request targets remain protected.
A renewed attack reopens retaliatory pressure immediately.

critique_rewrite_iteration.failure: The first rewrite rotated repeats to fresh nonhostile rivals. In the exact full replay it kept all 10 target actions and increased unique actor-target pairs from 6 to 10.
critique_rewrite_iteration.correction: The second rewrite blocks a new nonhostile target while the current campaign target remains alive and nonallied.

cuts_considered.implemented: Remove nonretaliatory repeat marks and fresh-target rotation while a campaign target is still live, because replay concentration and the official -40 relation effect establish both reach and a direct cost.
cuts_considered.not_delete_all_alliance_requests: All 133 requests occur in losses, but weak-position selection confounds the outcome count and the action can still create legal protection. No new alliance rule was added.
cuts_considered.not_delete_all_holds: All 123 holds occur in losses, but a hold is safer than a social action that creates a known hostility penalty when every tactical option is exhausted.
cuts_considered.not_restore_subhalf_naval_invasions: The retained rci-3 boundary found zero sub-0.50 rival invasions among 464 historical winning invasions.
cuts_considered.not_cut_core_tactics: Attack, boat, build, upgrade, retreat, warship, and nuke actions all appear in winning episodes; outcome correlation alone does not justify removing them.

rejected_rci5_v1.verdict: rejected because it spread the same hostility budget across more rivals

rci_verdict.implementation: unit, container, qualifier, exact matched-parent, and full current-package replay checks passed
rci_verdict.local_direction: The correction cut target marks by 70 percent with the exact same winner, turn count, and final tiles; it added seven holds and did not establish a win-rate lift.
rci_verdict.standard_promotion_gate: not completed: no hosted 4/4 or 20/20 regression
rci_verdict.league_action: none; qd1n:v77 remains champion after round 411 rank 1 and round 412 rank 2
